analysis.summary: In Q1 FY27, Krishana Phoschem delivered a 35% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations to ₹532 crore, with EBITDA rising 36% to ₹89 crore and PAT increasing 54% to ₹47 crore. The operating environment was impacted by monsoon delays and geopolitical tensions in West Asia that disrupted raw material availability and inflated input costs. The company recently expanded its NPK-DAP manufacturing capacity by 165,000 MT to reach a total capacity of 495,000 MT. Management expressed confidence in achieving 30%-35% top-line growth over last year and targeting quarterly revenues exceeding ₹500 crore over the remaining quarters of FY27. Krishana Phoschem Limited reported its Q1 FY27 financial results, with quarterly revenue growing 34.58% YoY to ₹532.3 crore and Profit After Tax rising 53.88% YoY to ₹47.06 crore.

guidance.claim: Krishana Phoschem targets achieving an additional 30% to 35% revenue turnover growth over the previous year.
guidance.quote: We are hoping that over the remaining quarters, we will be able to smoothen our production, and we will be able to achieve an additional 30%–35% turnover over last year.

guidance.claim: The company expects to maintain a quarterly revenue run rate of over ₹500 crore for the remaining three quarters of FY27.
guidance.quote: We expect to achieve a quarterly turnover of more than ₹500 crore over the remaining three quarters of FY27, supported by improved capacity utilization and production.

guidance.claim: Peak utilization of current total capacity has the potential to generate total annual revenue of over ₹3,000 crore.
guidance.quote: Based on the capacity and the pricing I have mentioned, the total revenue potential can be more than ₹3,000 crore.

guidance.claim: The company expects to deliver growth of over 40% across key parameters during the current year.
guidance.quote: Accordingly, we expect to deliver growth of over 40% across key parameters during the current year.

guidance.claim: Management projects a top-line revenue increase of around Rs. 500 crore from expanded capacity and asset utilization.
guidance.quote: So, you expect an increase of around Rs. 500 crore more, Rs. 2,900 to Rs. 3,000. But this is all numbers based on the capacity expanded and the utilization of that asset.

guidance.claim: Overall revenue growth of 35% to 40% is expected in FY27 including imports and manufacturing.
guidance.quote: Yes, including the import and manufacturing we expect 40% growth should not be a big issue.

guidance.claim: For FY27, the company expects to import around 150,000 metric tons of material, translating to approximately Rs. 1,000 crore in revenue.
guidance.quote: For FY27, based on market demand, we expect to import around 150,000 metric tons of material, which would translate into approximately Rs.1,000 crore of revenue.

demand_outlook.claim: Monsoon revival, higher crop MSPs, and NBS subsidy support are expected to sustain fertilizer demand through FY27.
demand_outlook.quote: Improving in monsoon conditions, higher MSP and continued government support through the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) framework are expected to support the fertilizer demand during the remainder of FY27.

demand_outlook.claim: In Q1 FY27, the company sold 53,500 MT of NPK-DAP and 36,300 MT of SSP.
demand_outlook.quote: For NPK-DAP, it was 53,500 MT, for SSP 36,300 MT

demand_outlook.claim: Stable demand dynamics were witnessed during the Rabi season for the quarter ended March 2026.
demand_outlook.quote: On the Rabi season, the quarter ended March ‘26, witnessed stable demand dynamics during the Rabi season.

demand_outlook.claim: Industry P&K production reached 15.76 lakh metric tonne during the peak period.
demand_outlook.quote: This was reflected in strong industry performance with P&K production reaching 15.76 lakh metric tonne during the peak period, marking one of the highest monthly output levels.

demand_outlook.claim: A favorable monsoon outlook and stable agricultural environment provide a constructive demand outlook.
demand_outlook.quote: On one hand, a stable agricultural environment supported by a favorable monsoon outlook provides a constructive demand outlook.

capex_expansion.claim: The company added 165,000 MT of NPK-DAP capacity, bringing total NPK-DAP capacity to 495,000 MT.
capex_expansion.quote: Our existing NPK-DAP capacity is 330,000 MT, and we have added another 165,000 MT, taking the total capacity to 495,000 MT.

capex_expansion.claim: Krishana Phoschem is currently evaluating potential capacity expansion opportunities.
capex_expansion.quote: We are currently evaluating certain capacity expansion opportunities.

capex_expansion.claim: The third-party green ammonia arrangement for 70,000 MTPA with SECI will commence supply in FY29.
capex_expansion.quote: And this capacity will start in FY29 after 2 years.

capex_expansion.claim: Expanded capacities at Meghnagar for NPK/DAP at 165,000 MTPA and Sulphuric Acid at 99,000 MTPA are contributing progressively to performance.
capex_expansion.quote: Our expanded capacities at Meghnagar — NPK/DAP at 165,000 MTPA and Sulphuric Acid at 99,000 MTPA — are now contributing progressively to our performance.

capex_expansion.claim: Total phosphatic fertilizer capacity was expanded to 615,000 MTPA, including NPK/DAP capacity enhancement to 495,000 MTPA.
capex_expansion.quote: NPK/DAP capacity enhanced by 50% to 495,000 MTPA and existing SSP capacity at 120,000 MTPA, taking total phosphatic fertilizer capacity to 615,000 MTPA

capex_expansion.claim: Backward integration capacity for sulphuric acid was strengthened to 99,000 MTPA.
capex_expansion.quote: Backward integration strengthened with sulphuric acid capacity of 99,000 MTPA

capex_expansion.claim: Krishana Phoschem signed a 10-year Green Ammonia Sale Agreement for 70,000 MTPA under the National Green Hydrogen Mission.
capex_expansion.quote: As part of our long-term sustainability strategy, Krishana Phoschem has entered into a 10-year Green Ammonia Sale Agreement (GASA) under India’s National Green Hydrogen Mission for 70,000 MTPA.

margins_costs.claim: Q1 FY27 EBITDA reached ₹89 crore, registering a 36% year-on-year growth.
margins_costs.quote: Quarterly EBITDA stood at ₹ 89 crore, reflecting a 36% year-on-year growth, supported by disciplined cost management, despite volatility in raw material prices.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA margin stands at roughly 7%–8% for trading operations and around 16% for manufacturing.
margins_costs.quote: The EBITDA margin is approximately 7%–8% for trading and around 16% for manufacturing.

margins_costs.claim: Management passed on roughly 25% to 30% of raw material cost increases via subsidy support and revised selling prices.
margins_costs.quote: Overall, we have been able to pass on ~ 25%–30% of the increase in input costs.

margins_costs.claim: Sulphur prices surged from ₹65,000–₹70,000 per tonne in April to nearly ₹1 lakh per tonne in June and July.
margins_costs.quote: Sulphur prices have risen from around ₹65,000–₹70,000 per tonne in April to almost ₹1 lakh per tonne in June and July.

margins_costs.claim: Quarterly revenue grew 34.58% YoY to ₹532.3 crore due to sustained capacity utilization and efficient execution.
margins_costs.quote: Quaterly revenue grew 34.58% YoY to ₹532.3 crore, driven by sustained capacity utilization and efficient execution across our integrated value chain.

margins_costs.claim: Quarterly Profit After Tax grew 53.88% YoY to ₹47.06 crore due to improved operating efficiency and cost control.
margins_costs.quote: Quaterly Profit After Tax grew 53.88% YoY to ₹47.06 crore, reflecting improved operating efficiency and disciplined cost control.

margins_costs.claim: Q4 FY26 EBITDA reached Rs. 90 crore, up 59% YoY due to operating leverage and stable cost management.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA came in at Rs.90 crore, registering a 59% YoY growth, supported by operating leverage from higher volumes and stable cost management despite input price volatility.

margins_costs.claim: Full-year FY26 EBITDA increased by 62% YoY to Rs. 298 crore.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA increased to Rs.298 crore, up 62% YoY, supported by improved operating performance, and a favourable product mix.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA per ton on the manufacturing side in FY26 was in the range of Rs. 5,500 per ton.
margins_costs.quote: It was in the range of Rs.5,500 per ton.

margins_costs.claim: Operating profit margins are expected to be under pressure as FY26 margin levels may not be fully sustainable.
margins_costs.quote: As mentioned earlier, margins will be under pressure, and the levels achieved in FY26 may not be fully sustainable.

orders_capacity.claim: Krishana Phoschem achieved total fertilizer production of 89,747 metric tonnes in Q1 FY27.
orders_capacity.quote: Achieved fertilizer production of 89,747 metric tonnes, showcasing our consistent operational efficiency.

orders_capacity.claim: Q1 FY27 capacity utilization stood at 43% for NPK-DAP and 121% for the SSP unit.
orders_capacity.quote: 43% capacity utilization of NPK-DAP unit and 121% capacity utilization of SSP unit, which was beyond the core.

orders_capacity.claim: The company has an installed manufacturing capacity of 6.15 Lakh MTPA.
Fertilizer production reached 94,103 MT in Q4 FY26.
orders_capacity.quote: Achieved fertilizer production of 94,103 MT, driven by peak Rabi season demand and improved operational throughput

orders_capacity.claim: Total fertilizer production achieved for FY26 was 397,263 MT.
orders_capacity.quote: Achieved total production of 397,263 MT, supported by High demand across markets

orders_capacity.claim: In FY26, trading volumes were approximately 93,000 metric tons while manufacturing volumes were around 383,000 metric tons.
orders_capacity.quote: Trading volumes were approximately 93,000 metric tons, while manufacturing volumes were around 383,000 metric tons.

capital_allocation.claim: The company executed a 5-for-1 stock split, subdividing face value from ₹10 to ₹2 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: Recently, the company successfully executed a 5-for-1 stock split, subdividing the face value of our equity shares from ₹ 10 per share to ₹ 2 per share.

capital_allocation.claim: Debtors collections during the quarter exceeded ₹700 crore.
capital_allocation.quote: Collection is more than Rs. 700 crore.

capital_allocation.claim: Depreciation increased to ₹13 crore and finance costs rose to ₹20 crore due to newly commissioned capacity.
capital_allocation.quote: Depreciation increased from around ₹8.7 crore to ₹13 crore, while finance costs increased from around ₹13 crore to ₹20 crore.

capital_allocation.claim: The Cabinet approved NBS rates for Kharif 2026 along with a fertilizer subsidy outlay exceeding ₹2.4 lakh crore for FY27.
capital_allocation.quote: The Cabinet's approval of NBS rates for Kharif 2026, alongside a fertilizer subsidy outlay exceeding ₹2.4 lakh crore for FY27, underscores the government's commitment to farmer affordability & sector stability.

capital_allocation.claim: The capacity expansion was funded through a mix of internal accruals and term loans.
capital_allocation.quote: This expansion has been funded through a prudent mix of internal accruals and term loans, reflecting disciplined capital allocation.

capital_allocation.claim: CRISIL upgraded the credit rating of Krishana Phoschem to A+ (Stable).
capital_allocation.quote: We are also pleased to highlight that our credit rating has been upgraded by CRISIL to A+ (Stable), reflecting improved financial strength and business fundamentals

risks_headwinds.claim: A 40% rainfall deficit by late June led to a 22.7% year-on-year drop in national Kharif sowing.
risks_headwinds.quote: By the end of June, cumulative rainfall was nearly 40% below normal, resulting in national Kharif sowing declining by 22.7% year-on-year to 182.7 lakh hectares, compared to 236.5 lakh hectares during the corresponding period last year.

risks_headwinds.claim: West Asia shipping uncertainties increased freight expenses, delayed vessels, and raised procurement costs.
risks_headwinds.quote: The uncertainty surrounding shipping routes resulted in higher freight costs, delay in vessel movement, and increased procurement costs.

risks_headwinds.claim: Raw material availability constraints posed the primary operational challenge in Q1 FY27.
risks_headwinds.quote: The primary challenge during the first quarter was the availability of raw materials.

risks_headwinds.claim: Global market input prices firmed from mid-February onwards due to supply constraints, gas production tightness, and higher freight costs.
risks_headwinds.quote: However, from mid-February onwards, global market witnessed firming trends driven by supply-side constraints, tightness in gas-linked production, higher logistic and freight costs.

risks_headwinds.claim: Rising input costs and slowing domestic demand in March created cost pressure in the closing quarter.
risks_headwinds.quote: This created a timing mismatch where domestic demand was slowed down in March while input costs were increasing, leading to higher cost pressure in the closing quarter.

management_commitments.claim: The company expects to generate more than ₹500 crore in quarterly turnover over the remaining three quarters of FY27.
management_commitments.quote: We expect to achieve a quarterly turnover of more than ₹500 crore over the remaining three quarters of FY27, supported by improved capacity utilization and production.

management_commitments.claim: Supply from the 70,000 MTPA green ammonia agreement is scheduled to start in FY29.
management_commitments.quote: And this capacity will start in FY29 after 2 years.

management_commitments.claim: Benefits of the expanded operational capacities are expected to meaningfully reflect in performance from FY27 onwards.
management_commitments.quote: With enhanced capacities now operational, we expect the benefits of this expansion to meaningfully reflect in our performance from FY27 onwards, supported by improved scale, operating leverage, and better efficiency levels.

management_commitments.claim: Supply under the green ammonia agreement is expected to commence after approximately three years.
management_commitments.quote: As per the contract, the green ammonia plant is expected to commence operations in the third year, so we expect supply after approximately three years.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
